answer: You can take trains from major Pakistani cities to Lahore. The main station connects to the western part of Pakistan, including Faisalabad. The Samjhauta Express used to run between Lahore and Attari, Amritsar, but services have been suspended since 2019 due to tensions. Local stations in Lahore include Shahdara Bagh, Badami Bagh, Moghalpur, Baghbanpura, Harbanspura, Jallo, and Wagah. For more information, you can visit the Lahore Art Gallery or the Al Hamra Arts Council.

There are routes from all major Pakistani cities to Lahore with Pakistan Railways official website. Trains from southern destinations (Multan, DG Khan, Karachi, etc.) and northern destinations (Gujrat, Gujranwala, Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, etc.) run from the main station. It also connects to the western part of Pakistan to Faisalabad and beyond. The Samjhauta Express (Friendship Express) ran twice a week between Lahore and Attari, Amritsar, across the border in India, however services have been suspended since 2019 by Pakistan citing tensions.

Local stations in Lahore are Shahdara Bagh, Badami Bagh, Moghalpura, Baghbanpura, Harbanspura, Jallo, and Wagah. These stations mostly have peak-hour services for commuters to Lahore.

Lahore has long been a bastion for sport. An excursion to a polo game would be a memorable experience. Pakistan is one of only 8 nations to play polo professionally, and fields some 26 professional clubs. Lahore's most famous club is Lahore Polo Club, where emperors, kings and other notables have been playing for centuries. Foreign teams often play here in friendly games, and facilities are first rate.

The Shalimar Gardens, another UNESCO World Heritage Site, reflect the Mughal tradition of formal gardens, fountains, and landscaped terraces.

Lahore also preserves buildings from the British colonial period, particularly along The Mall, where visitors can see historic institutions and architectural landmarks such as Lahore Museum and the General Post Office. The city offers a contrast between its older quarters and newer commercial districts, including Gulberg and Defence, which have modern shopping centres, restaurants, cafés, and hotels. Traditional bazaars, local cuisine, and cultural attractions make Lahore a destination for travellers interested in the history and everyday life of Pakistan.

Lahore (Punjabi: لہور; Urdu: لاہور‎) is Pakistan's second largest city after Karachi, and the capital of the north-eastern Punjab province. It is widely considered the country's cultural capital. The heart of Lahore is the Walled or Inner City, a very densely populated area of about one square kilometre.

Founded in legendary times, and a cultural centre for over a thousand years, Lahore has many attractions for the tourist. The Mughal and Sikh legacy survives in the Lahore Fort, Badshahi Mosque and Gurdwara, the Mall is lined with colonial-gothic buildings from the British Raj, and the suburbs of Gulberg and Defence feature palatial mansions and trendy shopping districts."},{"source_id":"Lahore > See > Mall Road","title":"Mall Road","text":"Lahore > See > Mall Road
